newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures finish mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures finish mostly higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mostly higher after a session spent on both sides of Wednesday's close.
September Standard and Poor's 500 futures ended up slightly, but they showed little conviction late in the day and traders called gains tentative.

Stock index futures had started the session strong, and September S&P 500s jumped the initial seven-point opening limit. September S&Ps soon climbed to 934.00, but spent the rest of the session in choppy trade and never regained that level.
Traders called afternoon trade light to moderate, and said a firm Treasury bond futures closed underpinned stock indices.

"Volume kind of died down a little bit," an S&P trader said of late action. "Earlier today on the way down it seemed like there was some commitment, but on the way back up volume has been really light," he said.
September S&Ps fell as low as 918.50 during the day, below 920.00 support but above Wednesday's 916.00 low.
September closed in the middle of its range and posted an inside day on daily bar charts, a signal of technical indecision in the market, traders said.
"We're in a negative situation, but they dashed the hopes of bears for now," another S&P 500 futures trader said. "We had a nice move down, but there was nothing violent in here at all," he said.
He noted afternoon support at 926.00 and 927.00.
The strong tone early in the day was tied to a T-bond rally and dollar strength on the latest batch of U.S. data.

The July consumer price index firmed 0.2 percent overall and in the core rate, matching market forecasts. Traders noted scant impact from other U.S. economic data Thursday morning, including industrial output and capacity use.
They were close to forecasts, coming in at a 0.2 percent rise in output and 83.1 percent for capacity use, off from 83.3 percent in June.

At the close, Sept S&Ps rose 2.25 pts to 928.05, Russell rose 1.50 to 414.25, Value Line added 3.00 to 837.25, NASDAQ rose 6.25 to 1111.50, Nikkei rose 290.0 to 19,395.0. ((Derivatives Desk (312) 408-8750)) E-mail:chicago.derivatives.newsroom@reuters.com
